tools.name: deleteApp
tools.title: Delete App

tools.description: Update an app (name / status / version)

tools.name: redeployApp
tools.title: Redeploy App
tools.description: Redeploy an app (refresh code + roll pods)

tools.name: createSshSession
tools.title: Create Ssh Session
tools.description: Create a short-lived SSH session credential for a running container

tools.name: execCommand
tools.title: Exec Command
tools.description: Run a one-off shell command in a running container (kubernetes exec)

tools.name: listBackups
tools.title: List Backups
tools.description: List an app's backups and its backup settings

tools.name: updateBackups
tools.title: Update Backups
tools.description: Turn managed backups on or off and set the daily window

tools.name: restoreBackup
tools.title: Restore Backup
tools.description: Overwrites the app's current volume contents with the snapshot. There is no undo.

tools.name: listBranches
tools.title: List Branches
tools.description: Fetched live from GitHub; empty for apps whose source is not git. `current` is the branch the app deploys from.

tools.name: rollbackDeploy
tools.title: Rollback Deploy
tools.description: Needs a running, build-backed app whose target image is still in the registry. Restarts every service in the instance, database included.

tools.name: getVolumeKeys
tools.title: Get Volume Keys
tools.description: Credentials are derived, not stored, so they are stable for the volume and need no rotation step. `volume` is a name from listVolumes.

tools.name: getDbCredentials
tools.title: Get Db Credentials
tools.description: Read from the running pod's resolved environment at call time, so the container is the source of truth rather than the template. `component` is a compose service running a database.

tools.name: getDbSchema
tools.title: Get Db Schema
tools.description: List a database component's schemas and tables

tools.name: runDbQuery
tools.title: Run Db Query
tools.description: Runs over a real protocol driver, not a shell, and executes whatever is sent — including writes and DDL. Redis and MongoDB take their own command syntax rather than SQL.

tools.name: getGitOverview
tools.title: Get Git Overview
tools.description: Reads the repository inside the running container by pod exec, so it is ground truth rather than the deploy record. Returns `{ok:false, reason}` when the app has no repo, no pod, or no git.

tools.name: runGitAction
tools.title: Run Git Action
tools.description: One action per call: discard, stage, unstage, commit, checkout, merge, rebase, revert, cherry, pull or push. Commits live in the container and die with it unless pushed.

tools.name: getGitDiff
tools.title: Get Git Diff
tools.description: With no `sha`, diffs the working tree. `path` narrows it to one file. Large patches come back with `truncated: true`.

tools.name: streamAppStatus
tools.title: Stream App Status
tools.description: Returns one status frame. Sending `Accept: text/event-stream` instead follows the status live, a frame every five seconds, which never completes on its own.

tools.name: streamAppMetrics
tools.title: Stream App Metrics
tools.description: Returns one metrics reading; `network` and `requestsPerSec` are null until a second sample exists, so they are null on a one-shot read. Sending `Accept: text/event-stream` instead follows usage live, a frame every five seconds, which never completes on its own.

tools.name: streamActiveDeploy
tools.title: Stream Active Deploy
tools.description: Returns one `{ts, deploy}` frame: the active deploy if one is running, otherwise the most recent, and `deploy` is null when the app has never deployed. Sending `Accept: text/event-stream` instead follows it live, a frame every two seconds, closing after one terminal frame.

tools.name: streamDeployLogs
tools.title: Stream Deploy Logs
tools.description: Returns one `{kind:"snapshot", log, status}` frame — the whole log so far, not a delta: the stored log for a finished deploy, the live build pod's log for the in-flight one. Sending `Accept: text/event-stream` instead re-sends a growing snapshot every two seconds; a finished deploy sends one frame and closes, the in-flight one keeps the connection open after it ends, so close it yourself once a frame carries `final: true`.

tools.name: deleteDomain

tools.name: updateDomain
tools.title: Update Domain
tools.description: Update a domain configuration

tools.name: listCertStatuses
tools.title: List Cert Statuses
tools.description: List TLS certificate statuses for app domains

tools.name: readServiceLogs
tools.title: Read Service Logs
tools.description: Returns the last 200 log lines of one container as `{container, state, logs}`; `state` is `no-pod` when nothing is running. `serviceName` is a compose service, or `clone` / `build` for an in-flight deploy's init steps. Sending `Accept: text/event-stream` instead follows the log live as server-sent events, one bare `data:` frame per line, which never completes on its own.

tools.name: getAppServices

tools.name: createS3Session

tools.name: endS3Session
